title: Flood risk
summary: A city's flood risk read from its own assessment: how deep each flood reaches on a 1 m map, which buildings it reaches, what the wards stand to lose each year, and how large a loss to expect once in so many years; with the hazards named for any place on Earth.

layers.title: how deep each flood reaches
layers.about: The depth of a flood at a return period, river or surface water, from JBA's maps of 1 m (taken here at about 4 m): the assessment's own hazard, on the ground.

layers.title: the buildings it reaches
layers.about: Of the assessment's 153,435 modelled buildings, those standing in over 15 cm at the flood chosen: columns on H3 cells by the value reached.

layers.title: what each ward stands to lose
layers.about: The average annual loss of each ward from the assessment's model, raised on its own ground, its height the loss per square kilometre.

layers.title: where the Council records floods
layers.about: The flash-flood places and areas recorded by the Freetown City Council: a check of the model by what the city has seen.

tools.title: What a flood costs the city
tools.about: The assessment's annual loss and its exceedance curves, its own figures beside what is recomputed here from its 1,943 modelled events.

tools.title: The hazards named for this place
tools.about: ThinkHazard!'s levels for an administrative unit: river and coastal floods, earthquakes, cyclones, landslides and others, by a name anywhere on Earth.

source: Freetown Flood Risk Assessment (World Bank, JBA Risk Management, Freetown City Council; CC BY 4.0); ThinkHazard! (GFDRR). The exposure is urban-science's, the curves tyche's.
